Place blocks side by side

bb_cols.Rd

Splits the available width into columns and places one block in each, top aligned by default. The row is as tall as its tallest fixed-height child; flexible children (plots without a height) stretch to that height.

Usage

bb_cols(
  ...,
  widths = NULL,
  gap = 0,
  valign = c("top", "center", "bottom"),
  sync_rows = FALSE,
  .list = NULL
)

Arguments

...

Blocks or anything [as_block()] accepts. `NULL` leaves the column empty.

widths

Column widths: `NULL`, numeric proportions or a unit vector.

gap

Space between columns (`grid::unit` or inches).

valign

Vertical alignment of shorter children: `"top"`, `"center"` or `"bottom"`.

sync_rows

Line up row heights of table children.

.list

Optional list of further children.

Value

A block.

Details

**Widths.** `NULL` gives equal columns. Numbers are proportions (`c(2, 1)`). A unit vector mixes absolute and proportional widths: `unit(c(3.25, 1), c("in", "null"))` takes 3.25 in for the first column and gives the rest to the second.

**Row sync.** With `sync_rows = TRUE`, children that are tables ([bb_table()]) get the same row heights, so dividers line up across columns. Shorter tables are padded with nothing; only existing rows grow.

Examples

bb_cols("Left", "Right", widths = c(2, 1), gap = 0.2)
#> <bb_cols>
